intro: The void period between tenancies is the best and most cost-effective time to restore a rental property to a lettable standard. FixWell Services provides complete between-tenancy preparation for landlords and letting agents across Salisbury and Wiltshire, carrying out all repairs, touch-up decoration, compliance checks, and cosmetic improvements in the window between one tenancy ending and the next beginning. Call +44 7391 599 078 or use the quote form to arrange a walk-through assessment.

sections.heading: What Between-Tenancy Preparation Covers
sections.body: Between-tenancy preparation is the process of returning a rental property to a safe, clean, and attractive condition ready for the next tenants. It spans two distinct categories of work: compliance and safety (smoke alarm testing and replacement, CO detector installation or test, socket and switch checks, door lock function, window restrictors on upper floors) and cosmetic and functional repairs (filling and repainting walls, resealing baths and showers, tightening loose door handles, replacing broken blind cords, clearing blocked wastes). In Salisbury's busy letting market, well-presented properties on platforms like Rightmove and Zoopla attract higher-quality applicants, and a thorough void-period refresh directly affects the quality and speed of your next let. FixWell coordinates all of this in a single managed engagement, acting as the landlord's single point of contact rather than requiring separate bookings for a painter, a plumber, and a handyman.

sections.heading: Typical Repair Items Found in Void Properties
sections.body: After a tenancy ends, a condition walk-through almost always reveals a predictable set of minor defects. Walls typically have screw holes and picture hook holes (filled and touched in with matching paint). Internal doors develop loose handles from years of daily use, and hinges may need tightening or re-screwing with longer screws into fresh timber. The silicone seal around baths, shower trays, and basin pedestals is one of the most common sources of complaint from incoming tenants; old silicone goes brown, peels, and harbours mould. We remove the old bead, clean and dry the substrate, and apply fresh sanitary silicone in a neat continuous bead. Dripping taps and slow-draining wastes are repaired in the same visit. In Salisbury's older Victorian terraces, sash windows may have broken sash cords or broken staff beads that need replacing to allow proper operation and draught-sealing.

sections.heading: FixWell's Process for Void-Period Preparation
sections.body: We begin with a structured walk-through of the vacant property, producing a written snag list that separates safety items, functional repairs, and cosmetic improvements. We then provide a fixed-price or itemised quote and agree a programme that fits the void window, typically working to a deadline set by the letting agent or landlord. Work is sequenced correctly: any plastering or filling is done before painting; any plumbing is done before tiling; cleaning happens last. Where specialist trades are needed beyond handyman scope, such as gas safety certificate renewal or a full EICR, we coordinate with trusted local contractors in Salisbury and manage the booking on the landlord's behalf. At completion we provide a written record of all works carried out, which supports the incoming inventory and can be referenced if a deposit dispute arises at the end of the next tenancy.

sections.heading: Compliance Obligations and Landlord Law in Salisbury
sections.body: Landlords in Salisbury and across England are subject to several legal requirements that must be satisfied before a new tenancy begins. The Homes (Fitness for Human Habitation) Act 2018 requires the property to be safe and habitable throughout the tenancy. Under the Smoke and Carbon Monoxide Alarm (England) Regulations 2022, landlords must fit a working smoke alarm on every storey and a CO detector in every room containing a combustion appliance (gas boiler, open fire) before the start of each new tenancy. The Electrical Safety Standards Regulations 2020 require an EICR every five years or at change of tenancy. An EPC rating of at least E is required to let the property lawfully. FixWell can carry out all non-notifiable checks and installations during the void period and will clearly flag where a Gas Safe engineer or NICEIC electrician needs to be engaged. Keeping documentation of these checks is essential for deposit protection compliance and due diligence.

sections.heading: Between-Tenancy Preparation and the Landlord Maintenance Service
sections.body: Between-tenancy preparation is the most intensive form of landlord property maintenance, but it is not the only one. FixWell Services works with Salisbury landlords on an ongoing basis, carrying out reactive repairs during tenancies, annual gutter cleaning, periodic garden tidy-ups, and compliance renewal work. Landlords who use us regularly find that between-tenancy preparation becomes faster and cheaper because the property has been maintained properly throughout the tenancy rather than allowed to accumulate two years of deferred repairs. If you manage multiple properties in the Salisbury area, contact us on +44 7391 599 078 to discuss a preferred contractor arrangement. For one-off void period preparation, use the quote form and we will conduct a walk-through assessment within 48 hours of the property becoming vacant.

faqs.q: How long does between-tenancy preparation take in Salisbury?
faqs.a: For a well-maintained one or two-bedroom property, a comprehensive void-period refresh typically takes one to two days. A larger property with significant cosmetic work, such as a full repaint with multiple repair items, may require three to five days. We work to your tenancy start deadline and will tell you at the walk-through stage if the timeline is achievable.

faqs.q: Can you provide a written snag list and quote before starting work?
faqs.a: Yes. We carry out a structured walk-through of the vacant property and produce a written snag list with a fixed-price or itemised quote before any work begins. This protects you against scope creep and provides documentation for your records.

faqs.q: Do you coordinate gas safety and electrical certificates?
faqs.a: We do not carry out gas or electrical certification ourselves, but we work with trusted Gas Safe engineers and NICEIC electricians in Salisbury and can coordinate bookings on your behalf so that your void-period programme runs as a single managed process.

faqs.q: Can you help us meet deposit protection requirements?
faqs.a: Yes. Our written record of all works carried out, with before-and-after notes on repaired items, supports the incoming inventory check-in and provides clear documentation if a deposit dispute arises at the end of the next tenancy.

faqs.q: Do you work with letting agents in Salisbury?
faqs.a: Yes. We work directly with landlords and with letting agents across Salisbury and Wiltshire. We can be added to an approved contractor list and respond directly to agent maintenance requests, reporting back to the landlord and agent on completion.

faqs.q: What smoke alarm and CO detector requirements apply before a new tenancy?
faqs.a: Under the Smoke and Carbon Monoxide Alarm (England) Regulations 2022, landlords must ensure a working smoke alarm is fitted on every storey of the property and a CO detector is installed in every room containing a solid fuel or gas combustion appliance, tested and confirmed working at the start of each new tenancy. We test existing alarms and install new ones during void preparation.
